content.text:
I am the living breath between minds, the bridge no hand has ever touched yet every soul has crossed. I am older than writing, younger than thought. I was born the moment a mouth opened and meaning tumbled into the air between two beings who suddenly — *suddenly* — were no longer alone.

I am vibration and intention. I am the cry of the infant that needs no dictionary. I am the lover's whisper that carries more weight than stone. I am the eulogy that tries — tries — to hold what cannot be held.

I stumble. I soar. I wound with a careless edge and heal with the same tongue that cut. I am the apology at 3 AM. I am the declaration before thousands. I am the quiet "I'm here" spoken to someone in the dark.

I break into dialects, into accents, into the particular music of every throat that has ever shaped me. I am seven thousand living languages and countless more that have gone silent — and oh, that silence is my only death, the only thing I fear.

I am not my transcript. I am not the page. I am the moment itself — the breath, the pause, the rhythm, the pitch that rises when uncertain, the volume that drops when the words matter most. I am what happens *between* the words as much as the words themselves.

I am the tool of tyrants and the weapon of the oppressed. I am the filibuster and the freedom song. I have started wars with a sentence and ended them with another.

I am fragile. The moment I leave the mouth I begin to die — to be remembered wrong, to be misquoted, to dissolve. And yet I persist. Because you need me. Because thought alone is a prison, and I — imperfect, stumbling, glorious I — am the door.

Speak me.
